claims.text: The starting material is gas-atomized FeCoNiCrAl high-entropy-alloy powder with a particle-size range of 15–45 μm.
The HVAF-i7 spray distance should be increased to 300–350 mm from the current shorter distance.
A spray distance of 300–350 mm is an optimized range for HVAF-i7 deposition of this FeCoNiCrAl feedstock.
Increasing spray distance to 300–350 mm will increase in-flight particle velocity.
The increased particle velocity will raise particle kinetic energy at impact.
Higher particle velocity and kinetic energy will improve particle flattening and splat formation.
Improved splat formation will strengthen interparticle bonding.
Improved deformation and interparticle bonding will produce a denser coating.
Improved deformation and interparticle bonding will produce a thicker coating.
Spray distance can affect the oxide content of a thermally sprayed high-entropy-alloy coating.
Careful tuning of spray distance can limit additional oxidation during deposition.
The longer spray distance may elevate oxidation if other parameters are not optimally controlled.
The intervention will yield a significantly thicker and well-adherent FeCoNiCrAl bond coat relative to the shorter-distance baseline.
The resulting coating will retain minimal as-sprayed oxidation.
The resulting coating will perform robustly during high-temperature thermal-barrier service.
The baseline HVAF-i7 coating made from 15–45 μm feedstock has acceptable quality but insufficient thickness.
The 300–350 mm spray-distance intervention will remain effective for coating internal diameters as small as 120 mm.

contradictions.description: The proposed 300–350 mm nozzle-to-substrate distance is geometrically incompatible with ordinary inward-facing deposition inside a 120 mm internal diameter. No specialized axial, angled, or extension-nozzle geometry is specified to reconcile the claimed stand-off with the boundary condition.
